tables.name: Table 1
tables.caption: ConvHull test accuracy results with the baseline PtrNet and different setups of the . The scale has been set to 3 for n=100 and 4 for n=200. At row 2 we observe that when the split block is not trained we get worse performance than the baseline, however, the generalization error shrinks faster on the baseline. When both blocks are trained jointly, we clearly outperform the baseline. In Row 3 the split is only trained with REINFORCE, and row 4 when we add the computational regularization term (See Supplementary) enforcing shallower trees.
tables.label: convexhull_results

tables.name: Table 2
tables.caption: We have used points for the Gaussian dataset and for the CIFAR-10 patches. The baseline performs better than the when the number of clusters is small but scales better with the number of clusters. When Lloyd's performs much better than its recursive version ("Gaussian" with ), we observe that performance is between the two. This shows that although having a recursive structure, is acting like a mixture of both algorithms, in other words, it is doing better than applying binary clustering at each scale. achieves the best results in the CIFAR-10 patches dataset, where Lloyd's and its recursive version perform similarly with respect to the k-means cost.

tables.name: Table 3
tables.caption: Performance Ratios of different models trained with (and using 3 splits in the ) and tested for (and different number of splits). We report the number of splits that give better performances at each for the . Note that for the model does best with 3 splits, the same as in training, but with larger more splits give better solutions, as would be desired. Observe that even for , the architecture significatively outperforms the non-recursive model, highlighting the highly constrained nature of the problem, in which decisions over an element are highly dependent on previously chosen elements. Although the clearly outperforms the baseline and the Dantzig algorithm for , its performance eventually degrades at ; see text.
